answer: Operator Device Anomaly Tax is the core rule. A hidden beacon in the hardware logs the physical CPU frequency drift during every transaction. If a network monitor detects a ripple of identical drift patterns across multiple nodes, it flags the entire cluster as a single operator. Each compromised identity then triggers a mandatory payment of the falcon fee to a public blacklist. This drains the attacker’s private treasury for every fake agent they deploy. The cost scales linearly with volume, making mass deployment financially ruinous.
